title: AFCAT Exam Guide: Flying, Technical & Ground Duty Officer Careers
summary: Everything you need to know about the Air Force Common Admission Test (AFCAT) for men and women: syllabus, cutoff trends, AFSB interview, and pilot training.
author: Sarkari Aavedan Editorial Team
content:
## Introduction

The Air Force Common Admission Test (AFCAT) is conducted twice a year by the Indian Air Force (IAF) to select graduate men and women as commissioned Class-I Gazetted Officers in the Flying Branch, Ground Duty (Technical) Branch, and Ground Duty (Non-Technical) Branch. Training takes place at the prestigious Air Force Academy (AFA) Dundigal, Hyderabad, leading to commission as Flying Officers with soaring leadership opportunities.

## Branch-Wise Eligibility Criteria

| Branch | Educational Qualifications | Minimum Marks Required |
|---|---|---|
| **Flying Branch** | Graduate in any discipline with minimum 60% marks AND passed 10+2 with minimum 50% marks each in **Maths and Physics** OR B.E. / B.Tech degree with min 60% marks. | 60% in Graduation & 50% in 10+2 Maths/Physics |
| **Ground Duty (Technical) - Aeronautical Engineer (Electronics / Mechanical)** | 10+2 with minimum 50% marks in Physics and Mathematics AND minimum 4-year degree in Engineering/Technology from a recognized University with min 60% marks. | 60% in Engineering Degree |
| **Ground Duty (Non-Technical) - Weapon Systems (WS) Branch** | 10+2 with minimum 50% marks in Maths & Physics AND Graduation in any discipline with min 60% marks. | 60% in Graduation |
| **Ground Duty (Non-Technical) - Administration & Logistics** | Graduate in any discipline from a recognized University with minimum 60% marks or equivalent. | 60% aggregate score in Graduation |
| **Ground Duty (Non-Technical) - Accounts** | B.Com / B.B.A (Finance) / B.M.S / B.B.S / C.A. / C.M.A. with minimum 60% marks. | 60% in Commerce / Finance Degree |
| **Ground Duty (Non-Technical) - Education** | 10+2 and Post-Graduation with 50% in any discipline including integrated courses AND 60% in Graduation. | 50% PG + 60% UG |

## Age Limit & Marital Status

| Branch | Permissible Age Limit | Marital Status Rules |
|---|---|---|
| **Flying Branch** | 20 - 24 Years (Up to 26 years for valid DGCA Commercial Pilot Licence holders) | Unmarried below 25 years of age |
| **Ground Duty (Technical & Non-Technical)** | 20 - 26 Years | Unmarried below 25 years of age (Married allowed if above 25 years) |

## AFCAT Examination Pattern

| Section / Subject | Number of Questions | Maximum Marks | Time Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General Awareness** | 20 Questions | 60 Marks | Combined 2 Hours (120 Minutes) |
| **Verbal Ability in English** | 30 Questions | 90 Marks | (3 marks awarded for correct answer, |
| **Numerical Ability (Mathematics)** | 20 Questions | 60 Marks | 1 mark deducted for incorrect answer) |
| **Reasoning and Military Aptitude Test** | 30 Questions | 90 Marks | Total Questions: 100 Questions |
| **Grand Total** | **100 Questions** | **300 Marks** | **2 Hours (Typical cutoff: 140 - 165 Marks)** |

## Air Force Selection Board (AFSB Interview) Stages

| Stage | Testing Procedure | Evaluated Skills |
|---|---|---|
| **Stage-I (Day 1)** | Screening Test | Officer Intelligence Rating (OIR) test and Picture Perception & Discussion Test (PPDT). Screened-out candidates return home the same day. |
| **Stage-II (Day 2-5)** | Psychological Tests | Thematic Apperception Test (TAT), Word Association Test (WAT), Situation Reaction Test (SRT), Self Description (SD). |
| **Group Tests (GTO)** | Outdoor Ground Activities | Group Discussion (GD), Military Planning Exercise (MPE), Progressive Group Task (PGT), Half Group Task (HGT), Individual Obstacles, Snake Race, Command Task. |
| **Personal Interview** | Board Interview | Deep assessment of personal background, academic record, current affairs, defense knowledge, and decision-making by Interviewing Officer. |
| **CPSS (Computerised Pilot Selection System)** | For Flying Branch Only | One-in-a-lifetime test consisting of instrument reading test and machine sensor test. If cleared, candidate is permanently eligible for military flying. |

## High-Scoring Preparation Strategy

| Phase | Action Plan & Regimen |
|---|---|
| **Phase 1: English & Reasoning Focus (60% Weightage)** | English (30 Qs) and Reasoning (30 Qs) comprise 180 out of 300 marks. Practice error spotting, idioms, cloze test, dot situation problems, figure classification, and Venn diagrams. Target 150+ marks from these two sections alone. |
| **Phase 2: Numerical Ability Speed** | AFCAT maths focuses on arithmetic: Decimals & Fractions, Time & Work, Decimal Fractions, Profit & Loss, Ratio & Proportion, Simple Interest, Speed Time & Distance, Trains, and Boats & Streams. Solve 20 questions daily to score 50+ marks. |
| **Phase 3: Aviation & Defense GK** | Learn names of IAF fighter jets (Rafale, Su-30MKI, Tejas, Mirage 2000), transport aircraft (C-17, C-130J, AN-32), helicopters (Apache, Chinook, Mi-17V5), air exercises, and missile arsenals (BrahMos, Astra, Akash). |
| **Phase 4: Previous Year Mocks & Time Management** | Solve 15 official previous year papers. Since time is generous (120 minutes for 100 questions), focus heavily on accuracy to eliminate negative penalties. |

Becoming an officer in the Indian Air Force gives you the privilege to touch the sky with glory. Build sharp mental aptitude, cultivate Officer Like Qualities (OLQs), and aim for high written cutoffs to ensure your place on the merit list.
